title: Sony Bags TV Rights for India-Afghanistan T20I Series as Ganesh Chaturthi Schedule Push Adds New Twist
excerpt: The three-match Delhi series in September marks Afghanistan's first time officially hosting India in bilateral T20Is, while the schedule clash effectively ends the proposed India-Bangladesh tour.
body:
• Sony Sports Network has secured television rights for the India-Afghanistan T20I series after beating JioStar and Zee Unite8 in negotiations, with FanCode holding digital rights.
  • The three-match series is scheduled for September 13, 15, and 17 at Delhi's Arun Jaitley Stadium, marking the first time Afghanistan officially hosts India in a bilateral T20I series.
  • ITW Universe founder Bhairav Shanth has formally requested the Afghanistan Cricket Board to shift one match to September 14, Ganesh Chaturthi, calling it a gesture of goodwill toward Indian fans.
  • The confirmed schedule effectively ends India's proposed white-ball tour of Bangladesh, which had targeted the same September window.

Sony Wins the Rights Race

Sony Sports Network has won the television broadcast rights for India's upcoming three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, Cricbuzz reported on Thursday. The ITW Universe, which holds the global rights for the series, allotted the property to Sony after deliberations with rival bidders JioStar and Zee Unite8.

FanCode has secured the digital streaming rights for the matches. A top official at ITW Universe confirmed the deal to Cricbuzz.

The rights allocation comes ahead of what is expected to be a commercially significant series — India's first bilateral T20I engagement with Afghanistan, hosted by the Afghan board on Indian soil.

Schedule Confirmed, With a Festival Twist

The Afghanistan Cricket Board confirmed the series schedule in a formal letter to stakeholders on August 10, locking in September 13, 15, and 17 as match days. All three T20Is will be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi, with the BCCI's formal approval.

But ITW Universe founder Bhairav Shanth has written to ACB CEO Naseeb Khan requesting a schedule adjustment so that one match falls on September 14 — Ganesh Chaturthi, one of India's most widely observed festivals.

"Ganesh Chaturthi is one of the most widely observed and emotionally significant festivals in India — a day of new beginnings, devotion and collective celebration. By offering to stage a match on this date, the Afghanistan Cricket Board would be making a thoughtful and gracious gesture that goes beyond the playing field."

— Bhairav Shanth, Founder, ITW Universe

Shanth proposed two alternative schedules: September 11, 13, and 14 as the preferred option, or September 13, 14, and either September 16 or 17 as a fallback. Both configurations would preserve the tight three-match window while adding a holiday-boosted match day.

A Historic First for Afghanistan Cricket

The series marks the first time the Afghanistan Cricket Board will officially serve as the host nation for a bilateral T20I series against India. While Afghanistan has played home fixtures in both India and the UAE in recent years due to security concerns following the Taliban's takeover in 2021, this is the first time the ACB is formally hosting rather than simply playing in India.

"This series holds great significance for Afghanistan cricket and represents another important step in the development of our longstanding relationship with the BCCI," ACB Chairman Mirwais Ashraf said in a statement reported by Reuters.

BCCI president Mithun Manhas said the board was "committed to supporting the growth of cricket in Afghanistan" and would "continue to support Afghanistan cricket while strengthening the relationship between the two cricketing nations."

The two sides last met in June, when India beat Afghanistan by an innings and 300 runs in a one-off Test before sweeping the three-match ODI series 3-0.

Bangladesh Tour All But Dead

The confirmation of the Afghanistan series schedule has effectively killed India's proposed white-ball tour of Bangladesh. The Bangladesh Cricket Board had earmarked a September 1-13 window for six white-ball matches, but at least one Afghanistan match clashes with that slot.

The India-Bangladesh bilateral series was originally scheduled for August 2025 but was postponed amid political unrest in Bangladesh and strained relations between Dhaka and New Delhi. Tensions deepened after Bangladesh pacer Mustafizur Rahman was dropped by Kolkata Knight Riders from the IPL, prompting Bangladesh to boycott its World Cup matches in India.

While the election of a new BNP government in Bangladesh had raised hopes of a revival, ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina's press conference in India in early August further complicated diplomatic ties.

Looking Ahead: Asian Games Warm-Up

Both India and Afghanistan will use the T20I series to fine-tune their squads ahead of the Asian Games, which begin in late September. For Afghanistan, the series also carries commercial significance — the TV rights deal with Sony ensures broad visibility in the Indian market, while the Ganesh Chaturthi scheduling request signals the commercial partners' awareness of maximizing viewership on a holiday.

Whether the ACB adjusts the schedule remains to be seen, but the series itself is locked in as one of the key fixtures on the pre-Asian Games cricket calendar.
nri_angle: Indian cricket fans abroad can watch on Sony Sports and FanCode; the Ganesh Chaturthi match would coincide with a major diaspora festival celebration.
